_schema.purpose: The cross-driver rendering fixture for the `gwz local list` path column (LCM1.1 fix 3, lane C, 2026-09-06). Both drivers join `LocalFamilyResponse.root_path` (the family root as core observed it, design section 7 tag 3) with each member's root-relative `path` for the human table, and both implement the join lexically -- a parent reference cancels the named segment before it, nothing is read from the filesystem, no symlink is followed, no path is canonicalised. Nothing tested that the two joins agree; this file does. Both drivers read THIS file and assert every case against their own join; neither restates the cases inline and neither keeps a copy. Add a case here, not in a driver's test module.

_schema.rule: `expected` is the display path for the row: `root_path` joined with `path`, then parent and current-directory references resolved lexically. An absent (null) or empty `root_path` leaves `path` exactly as the wire carried it (a driver that does not know the root does not invent one). A `path` that is already absolute replaces the root rather than nesting under it. A parent reference cancels a preceding named segment only; above a relative root it stays in the answer, and at a filesystem root it is the root itself.
_schema.separators: Paths are spelled with `/`, the wire's own spelling of a member path (`gwz_family_model::normalize`). A driver whose native separator differs renders with its own separator and compares after mapping it to `/`; neither driver's suites run on such a host today (both Windows CI legs build and package only), so the mapping is a stated allowance, not a measured one.

cases.root_path: `LocalFamilyResponse.root_path` as core sent it: a string, or null for absent
cases.path: `LocalFamilyMemberEntry.path`, root-relative as the wire carries it
cases.expected: the display path both drivers must render

_schema.stability: Keys and case ids are stable. Append cases; do not renumber, rename or reorder existing ones. If the two drivers disagree on a case, that is a finding to report, never a reason to bend the expected value to one of them.

cases.note: A path with no parent reference nests under the root. The join does not judge whether such a member is admissible; core did that when it recorded the row.
Design section 8.1: the root's own row carries `.`, and renders as the root's directory.
The default destination `../<root-dirname>-<Name>` (design section 4, section 11 item 3): one parent reference cancels the root's last segment.
Each parent reference cancels one named segment; the model records such a path normalised, and the join resolves the run it records.

`root_path` is present exactly when `members` is (design section 7); a populated listing without one is a core that has not caught up, and the relative path is shown unchanged rather than joined with a guess.
An empty root is treated as absent: nothing to join against.
The wire never carries an absolute member path (the model records root-relative paths only), but a join must not nest one under the root if it ever does.
A trailing separator on the observed root is not a segment.
Not a normalised member path, but the join resolves every parent reference lexically, wherever it sits.
A relative observed root: the first parent reference cancels `gwz-dev`, the second has nothing named to cancel and stays in the answer.
At a filesystem root a parent reference is the root itself, as the operating system resolves it.
